new.claim: The admission in [A1] supplies stored $K,b$ equal to the intended data; the factorization and transformed right-hand side are therefore admissible stored operands. By [F4], $K$ is nonsingular and, being square, has full column rank, so the perturbation equations of [F2] apply under [A1]. Their additional perturbed-least-squares uniqueness condition is not needed for this residual calculation. Multiplying the triangular equation by $\widehat Q$ and using $\widehat Q\widehat Q^T=I$ gives $\widehat Q(\widehat R+\Delta_R)\widehat z=b+\delta b$. Substituting $\widehat Q\widehat R=K+\Delta_Q$ yields $(K+\Delta_K)\widehat z=b+\delta b$ for $\Delta_K=\Delta_Q+\widehat Q\Delta_R$. Orthogonality gives $\|\widehat Q\Delta_R\|_F=\|\Delta_R\|_F$, and $\|\widehat R\|_F=\|K+\Delta_Q\|_F\le(1+\beta_Q)\|K\|_F$. Hence $$\|\Delta_K\|_F\le \bigl(\beta_Q+\gamma_{N+3}(1+\beta_Q)\bigr)\|K\|_F =\beta_K\|K\|_F.$$ Rearrangement now gives $$\|K\widehat z-b\|_2\le \|\delta b\|_2+\|\Delta_K\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2 \le\beta_b\|b\|_2+\beta_K\|K\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2.$$

By [F3] and the triangle inequality, $$\|K\widehat z-b\|_2\le\|\widehat r\|_2+W.$$ Both entries in the returned minimum are upper bounds, so their minimum is also an upper bound. Failure of any required operation exits without a certificate.
